bull.b: High forward occupancy and advanced bookings provide meaningful revenue visibility across the next several sailing seasons. The growth in 2027 bookings and capacity indicates sustained demand for Viking’s itineraries, supporting pricing, planning confidence, and continued fleet investment.

Strong growth in revenue, EBITDA, and adjusted net income shows that Viking is converting demand and capacity expansion into operating leverage. Rising net yields and high occupancy support the durability of current earnings power, although performance remains tied to travel demand.

Adding purpose-built vessels expands Viking’s ability to serve established river itineraries while reinforcing its destination-focused product model. Fleet growth can increase capacity and itinerary choice over time, helping the company capture demand while building scale around its branded experience.

bear.b: A debt-heavy capital structure reduces financial flexibility if travel demand weakens or operating costs rise. Although recent earnings and liquidity have improved, substantial leverage increases debt-service exposure and can constrain capital allocation during a cyclical downturn.

Current cash generation is substantial, but the decline in free cash flow and weaker conversion from net income indicate that investment or working-capital needs absorb a meaningful portion of profits. Prior periods of negative free cash flow reinforce the business’s cyclical funding risk.

Dependence on European river itineraries exposes Viking to operating disruption when water levels are unusually low. Ship swaps, cancellations, vouchers, and added transportation costs can reduce future yields and create lingering pressure on reported results beyond the initial disruption.
